capabilities.name: HTTP client
capabilities.notes: Check async/runtime, target, proxy, TLS and streaming requirements; consolidate independent HTTP clients where possible.

capabilities.name: HTTP server framework
capabilities.notes: Hyper is a lower-level transport, not a competing framework.

capabilities.name: async runtime
capabilities.notes: Check platform and feature combinations; runtime adapters may be intentional.

capabilities.name: JSON implementation
capabilities.preferred: one implementation selected by API and performance requirements
capabilities.notes: Confirm that parsing and serialization workloads can share an implementation.

capabilities.name: TLS implementation
capabilities.preferred: btls from https://github.com/codeandsolder/btls-fast for compatible native TLS use
capabilities.notes: Platform-native TLS, certificate verification, pure Rust, or different protocol requirements may justify separate providers.

capabilities.name: QUIC transport
capabilities.preferred: quiche from https://github.com/codeandsolder/quiche-fast where protocol and runtime requirements fit
capabilities.notes: Check HTTP/3, runtime, platform and transport API requirements.

capabilities.name: terminal color
capabilities.notes: Consolidate direct color formatting; type interoperability may require an adapter.

capabilities.name: DEFLATE implementation
capabilities.preferred: zlib-rs from https://github.com/codeandsolder/zlib-rs-fast where streaming and format support fit
capabilities.notes: flate2 is a frontend and is not itself an additional provider; distinguish stream and whole-buffer workloads and C ABI requirements.

capabilities.name: regular expression engine
capabilities.preferred: one engine that meets the required syntax and performance
capabilities.notes: Lookaround, backreferences, ECMAScript compatibility and Unicode semantics may require distinct engines.

capabilities.name: argument parser
capabilities.notes: Check CLI API and platform requirements; parser combinators are distinct.

capabilities.name: version comparison
capabilities.notes: Retain a different comparator only for a genuinely different version grammar.

capabilities.name: Zstandard decoder
capabilities.notes: Pure Rust or WASM support can justify a second decoder.

capabilities.name: HTTP/2 transport
capabilities.preferred: one HTTP/2 implementation when transport APIs permit
capabilities.notes: Wreq and Hyper can use different transport APIs; do not blindly patch h2 to http2.

capabilities.name: mount wrapper
capabilities.preferred: existing nix or rustix mount API
capabilities.notes: Nix and Rustix cover many complementary syscalls; only libmount duplication requires investigation.

preferences.notes: Prefer the async Wreq client for compatible native applications. Migrate an owning dependency or use OpenDAL HttpTransport for storage; do not blindly substitute packages.

preferences.preferred: corresponding btls, btls-sys or tokio-btls package from https://github.com/codeandsolder/btls-fast
preferences.notes: Check BoringSSL binding and integration APIs; do not blindly substitute packages.
Check STEP parsing and entity API requirements.
CAD APIs have diverged; evaluate the corresponding implementation rather than assuming a drop-in replacement.

preferences.preferred: btls from https://github.com/codeandsolder/btls-fast where native BoringSSL TLS is suitable
preferences.notes: Prefer btls-fast for compatible native TLS; check certificate validation, platform trust and pure-Rust or WASM requirements. For adapters, migrate the owning HTTP/TLS dependency, not the adapter in isolation.
Use Axum routes, Tokio and bounded streaming; Hyper is the transport, not a competing framework.

preferences.preferred: btls-fast for compatible native cryptographic operations
preferences.notes: Avoid compiling a second native crypto implementation when the existing BoringSSL bindings provide the required primitives. For JWT, use jsonwebtoken-btls with built-in crypto providers disabled; for TLS migrate the owning stack. Benchmark/reference and pure-Rust or platform requirements may justify alternatives.
Use an existing syscall wrapper and preserve overlay escaping, mount flags and byte paths.
Use semver for version strings that follow SemVer, not arbitrary distribution version schemes.
Consolidate DEFLATE implementations when stream, format and ABI requirements permit; select flate2 zlib-rs rather than its default Miniz backend.

preferences.preferred: http2 from codeandsolder/cargo-patches where the Wreq transport is used
preferences.notes: h2 and the Wreq http2 fork are independent package identities. Do not substitute the fork into Hyper blindly; retain h2 if a separate HTTP/2 transport requires it.

preferences.preferred: zstd where native Zstandard is already used
preferences.notes: If the caller only parses archive metadata, disable unused object compression. Otherwise consolidate Zstandard decoders when target support and workload permit.

preferences.preferred: disable unused jsonwebtoken use_pem feature; otherwise retain ASN.1 support
preferences.notes: PEM parsing is unnecessary for callers using raw JWK components or DER keys. This is not a general ban on ASN.1 parsing.

preferences.preferred: Wreq webpki-roots/native-roots or an explicit btls certificate store
preferences.notes: Keep trust root representations aligned with the selected TLS stack; webpki-roots and webpki-root-certs are different representations, not drop-in replacements.

preferences.preferred: btls-fast RSA APIs for native consumers, including the shared Reqsign signing patch family
preferences.notes: Avoid a separate arbitrary-precision RSA signing backend when the application already uses BoringSSL. Reqsign core, Azure and Google must migrate as one family. For standalone, pure-Rust or WASM requirements evaluate the appropriate implementation rather than automatically replacing it.

preferences.preferred: lru for recency-bounded caches; indexmap for insertion-ordered maps
preferences.notes: Select based on actual ordered-map semantics. For weighted caches keep explicit weight accounting and eviction callbacks; do not replace an arbitrary linked map with a count-bounded cache.

preferences.preferred: Jiff for new date/time formatting and calendrical operations where compatible
preferences.notes: Consolidate if Jiff is already required. Evaluate supported timestamp range, time zones, serialization formats and WASM support before migrating; not a drop-in type alias.

feature_preferences.preferred: flate2 with the zlib-rs feature and a compatible codeandsolder/zlib-rs-fast Cargo patch
feature_preferences.notes: Keep the flate2 frontend when its API is useful; consolidate on the preferred DEFLATE backend if target and feature support permit. Verify the resolved zlib-rs source.

feature_preferences.preferred: jsonwebtoken-btls from codeandsolder/btls-fast; disable built-in crypto backends
feature_preferences.notes: For compatible native builds, install the btls provider and keep jsonwebtoken validation. Avoid a second native cryptographic stack. Retain other providers only when required by target or application.

feature_preferences.preferred: Disable use_pem if all keys already arrive as JWK components or DER
feature_preferences.notes: Review call sites before changing the feature; PEM callers need ASN.1 parsing. Removing unused PEM support eliminates simple_asn1 and its transitive dependencies.

feature_preferences.preferred: Disable object compression when only archive or executable metadata is required
feature_preferences.notes: Compressed debug sections require decompression; do not disable it for consumers that actually read them. Avoid the default Ruzstd backend when not needed.

feature_preferences.preferred: Disable default features when WebSocket server functions are unused; explicitly enable the required Tokio and Tower HTTP features
feature_preferences.notes: The default enables server_fn/axum and axum/ws, which pulls in tungstenite and tokio-tungstenite. Preserve axum-no-default HTTP server function support and actual static-file routes. Keep WebSockets when used.
